The finding’s specific "millisecond" claim isn’t shown in the diff, but the lack of conversion for datetime-based pagination is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — The PR silently removes the start/end/statsPeriod date filtering, so existing clients that pass date ranges now get unfiltered audit logs with no error (unrelated functional regression)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove or alter any start/end/statsPeriod date filtering logic in `organization_auditlogs.py`. The only changes shown are switching paginator imports, adding an optional `OptimizedCursorPaginator` path gated by `optimized_pagination` and admin access, and adding negative-offset handling in paginator/cursor utilities. No date-range filtering code is deleted or modified in the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The BasePaginator change affects every paginator: it silently clamps negative offsets for next-page cursors but still passes negative offsets through for is_prev cursors, so crafted prev cursors still 500 on every endpoint while the comment claims it is safe

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the new logic clamps negative `offset` only when `not cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), but for `is_prev` it still passes `offset` through even if negative. Django `QuerySet` slicing with negative indexes is not supported and can raise (commonly an `AssertionError`), so a crafted cursor with `is_prev=true` and a negative `offset` can still trigger a 500. This contradicts the added comment claiming the queryset will safely handle boundary conditions, and the change affects all endpoints using this paginator path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 — Passing `enable_advanced_features=True` through self.paginate relies on paginate forwarding unknown kwargs to the paginator constructor; if paginate does not forward them, this raises TypeError (base.py is not in this repo, so this could not be checked)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, enable_advanced_features=True)` was added in `organization_auditlogs.py`. Whether this works depends on `paginate` accepting/forwarding unknown kwargs to the paginator constructor; that behavior isn’t shown in this diff. If `paginate` doesn’t forward it, this could raise a `TypeError`, but that cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:890 — The prev-cursor trim compares against the unclamped `offset` rather than `start_offset`, so negative or clamped offsets make the trimming wrong and return extra or duplicate rows

adjudication.rationale: In both modified `get_result` implementations, `start_offset` is only clamped with `max(0, offset)` when `not cursor.is_prev`. The “prev-cursor trim” block (`if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:`) only runs when `cursor.is_prev` is true, and in that case `start_offset` is set to `offset` (i.e., not clamped). So the trim condition using `offset + limit + extra` is not mismatched against a clamped `start_offset` in the shown code paths; the finding’s premise (“unclamped offset rather than start_offset”) doesn’t align with the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removed start/end/statsPeriod query params and date-range filtering, silently breaking existing clients that filter audit logs by date (params now ignored, returning unfiltered results).

adjudication.rationale: The diff only modifies pagination behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (switching between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on `optimized_pagination` and admin/global access). It does not show removal of `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` query params or any deletion/alteration of date-range filtering logic—no such code changes appear in the provided hunks. Therefore the claim that date filtering was removed/ignored is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New undocumented `optimized_pagination` query param changes cursor semantics per-caller (int value cursors vs DateTimePaginator ms-timestamp cursors) with no versioning, so cursors from one mode are incompatible with the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `optimized_pagination` query param in `organization_auditlogs.get()` that switches the endpoint between `DateTimePaginator` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (`paginator_cls=...`). Since different paginator classes can produce/consume different cursor formats/semantics, cursors returned in one mode are not guaranteed to work in the other, and there is no visible versioning/compat layer in the diff. This is an API/contract concern rather than a directly provable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to a datetime key and value_from_cursor passes raw int to a datetime filter, so the opt-in response path errors (500) instead of returning the documented rows/cursor shape.

adjudication.rationale: The new opt-in path in `organization_auditlogs.py` uses `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering by `-datetime`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor/ceil` on `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then casts to `int`, which will raise a `TypeError` if that value is a `datetime` (as it would be for an audit log `datetime` field). Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value without converting it to a datetime-compatible type, making it very likely that `build_queryset(...)` (inherited) would apply an incompatible filter for a datetime key. This makes the optimized pagination branch plausibly crash (500) when exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator shared by all endpoints now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors, changing public cursor contract for every paginated API (negative slicing errors in Django rather than clamping).

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the change clamps negative offsets only for non-prev cursors: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For `cursor.is_prev`, it still uses `offset` directly, which is the same behavior as before (previously it always sliced with `queryset[offset:stop]` regardless of direction). So the diff does not introduce a new “now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors” contract change across all endpoints; if negative offsets were possible, they were already passed through previously.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — Negative cursor offsets are accepted as a public API capability ("access data beyond normal pagination bounds") without validation, widening the cursor contract clients can send.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code intentionally slices the queryset with a negative start (`results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` where `start_offset = cursor.offset`). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexing and will raise an error, and there is no validation/clamping of negative offsets in this path (contrast with the earlier `max(0, offset)` logic). This means negative cursor offsets can be accepted and can trigger broken behavior, effectively widening the cursor contract without safeguards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the `datetime` field (order_by="-datetime"), raising TypeError on every non-empty page when optimized_pagination=true

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then calls `math.floor/ceil(value)` before casting to `int`. If `self.key` corresponds to the ordered field (`datetime`), `value` will be a `datetime` object, and `math.floor/ceil` will raise `TypeError` on any non-empty result set. Nothing in the diff shows special handling to convert datetimes to a numeric cursor value (unlike a dedicated DateTime paginator would).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset compares against a DateTimeField, so cursor-based page navigation fails or filters wrongly

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `OptimizedCursorPaginator` into `organization_auditlogs.get()` with `order_by="-datetime"` (a DateTimeField). But `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` assumes the key value is numeric (`math.floor/ceil` and `int(...)`), and `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` without any DateTime parsing/conversion. With a datetime-ordered queryset, this will either error (numeric ops on datetime) or produce mismatched cursor values that won’t correspond to the datetime filtering done inside the inherited `build_queryset`, breaking cursor navigation/filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — Negative cursor offsets are passed straight to Django queryset slicing, which raises AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported"), producing a 500 instead of results

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/retains paths where a negative `cursor.offset` can be used directly in queryset slicing. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Also in the earlier paginator change it uses `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev`, which can also be negative. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and will raise an exception, leading to a 500 if a negative offset cursor is provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now skips clamping negative offsets for prev cursors, so any client-supplied cursor like "v:-5:1" crashes every cursor-paginated endpoint with a 500 (previous behavior was the same crash but this "fix" enshrines it and removes no guard)

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the diff introduces clamping for non-`is_prev` cursors (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). Previously *all* cursors used `queryset[offset:stop]` with no clamping at all, so negative offsets could already crash; the change does not newly “skip clamping” for prev cursors (there was no clamping before). The finding also cites a client cursor like `v:-5:1` implying a negative *offset*, but from the diff we can only see `Cursor(value, offset, is_prev)` and cannot verify that string encodes a negative offset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member can be None (e.g. staff/non-member access via OrganizationAuditPermission), so `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError for non-superusers without membership

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. Unlike the previous code path, this unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member` when the user is not a superuser. If `organization_context.member` can ever be `None`, this will raise `AttributeError` and break the endpoint for that access pattern. The diff provides no null-guard or fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod handling silently drops existing date-range filtering, so clients requesting a date window now get unfiltered audit logs

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (switching between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on query/user flags) and adds cursor/offset-related logic in paginator code. There is no shown removal or modification of any `start`, `end`, or `statsPeriod` request handling or queryset date-range filtering in the provided diff hunks, so the claim that date-window filtering was silently dropped is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 — Prev-cursor trimming compares len(results) to offset+limit+extra, but the slice length is based on start_offset, so the extra row is not trimmed when offsets differ (e.g. negative)

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` trimming check only runs under `if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:`. In all slicing paths that can reach that block, `start_offset` is set equal to `offset` (either `start_offset = cursor.offset` in the advanced negative-offset branch, or `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev` in the normal branch). The diff does not show any case where `start_offset` differs from `offset` for this trimming logic, so the stated mismatch (“slice length is based on start_offset, so trimming fails when offsets differ”) is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator used with order_by="-datetime" treats the datetime key as numeric (math.floor on datetime, raw int passed back as cursor value) instead of reusing DateTimePaginator's conversion, a type-boundary leak that breaks on first use

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new path uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. The added `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `int(math.floor(value) ... )`, which will fail if `value` is a `datetime` (Python `math.floor()` does not accept datetimes). Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, there is no datetime-to-numeric conversion, so this is a real type mismatch introduced by the diff and would break pagination when using the optimized path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — get_result copy-pastes nearly all of BasePaginator.get_result (hits, extra, prev trimming, build_cursor, post_query_filter), so the two will drift; only the slice offset differs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result(...)` which reimplements the full pagination flow (cursor init, limit clamping, `build_queryset`, hits counting, `extra` handling, prev trimming, reversing, `build_cursor`, `post_query_filter`) and only meaningfully changes the slice/offset handling (negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is on). This is a concrete maintainability issue because it duplicates logic already present in the existing paginator implementation and can drift over time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — Both branches of the enable_advanced_features/negative-offset if-else compute the same slice (offset is already negative-passthrough when is_prev), so the "advanced" branch is effectively redundant

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the non-advanced branch clamps `start_offset` to `max(0, offset)` when `not cursor.is_prev`, but passes `offset` through unchanged when `cursor.is_prev` (which could be negative). The “advanced” branch (`enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0`) allows negative offsets regardless of `is_prev`. Therefore the two branches are not necessarily computing the same slice; they differ at least when `cursor.is_prev` is false and `offset` is negative. The finding’s claim of redundancy (“both branches compute the same slice”) misreads this control flow and cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — Comments claim Django ORM handles negative slicing and that it is "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level"; Django raises on negative indexing, so the comments are misleading

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` the branch `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:` sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (negative slice start). If negative slicing is not supported by the ORM, this will raise at runtime for that path. Regardless of the comment, the diff explicitly introduces negative offsets into queryset slicing, which is a correctness risk (likely broken behavior) gated only by `enable_advanced_features` and a negative cursor offset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179 — Shared BasePaginator slicing changed for all paginators with a comment asserting the queryset "will handle boundary conditions", which is false for negative offsets and couples every paginator to this feature

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the diff does not actually enable negative offsets “for all paginators”: it clamps to `max(0, offset)` when `not cursor.is_prev`, and leaves `offset` unchanged only for `cursor.is_prev` (the same behavior as before for prev since the old code always used `offset`). The new comment about negative offsets being “safe” is arguably misleading, but the finding’s claim that the slicing change broadly couples every paginator to negative-offset behavior is not supported by what changed at line ~179.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — Unrelated removal of start/end/statsPeriod date filtering (and serializer fields) is bundled into a pagination PR, silently dropping an existing API feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior: it conditionally switches between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and adds support for (potentially) negative offsets in paginator/cursor code. There is no shown removal of `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` filtering logic or serializer field changes in `organization_auditlogs.py` (the only logic change in that file is the `optimized_pagination` flag and admin gating). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — Two near-identical self.paginate calls differ only by paginator class and one kwarg; should select paginator_cls/kwargs then call once

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly contains two similar self.paginate calls in the new if/else block (organization_auditlogs.py), but the finding is essentially a DRY/refactor suggestion (select paginator_cls/kwargs then call once). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — Docstring advertises "optimized query path", "streamlined boundary handling" and backward compatibility that the code does not implement (premature/speculative abstraction behind a flag always passed True)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a concrete behavior matching the docstring’s main claim (negative offset support) in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`. The assertion that the abstraction is “behind a flag always passed True” is also not strictly supported by the diff: the constructor default is `False`, and the endpoint only passes `enable_advanced_features=True` in one conditional path (`use_optimized and enable_advanced`). Claims like “optimized query path”/“streamlined boundary handling” are subjective marketing language and not verifiably false from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — Comment claims negative offsets are enabled here but the line below is unchanged int(offset); comment describes no behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds only a comment above `self.offset = int(offset)` in `Cursor.__init__` without changing the assignment. However, `int(offset)` already accepts negative values, so the comment is not contradicted by the code shown, and there is no verifiable behavioral defect introduced at that line. This is at most a documentation/nit issue, not a concrete diff-grounded problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:23 — Removing start/end/statsPeriod date-range filtering means audit log queries can no longer be time-bounded, forcing deep offset scans over an org's full high-volume audit history.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove any start/end/statsPeriod (date-range) filtering from organization_auditlogs.py. The only visible change in that endpoint is switching paginator selection based on `optimized_pagination` and admin access, and no query time-bounding logic is deleted or altered in the shown hunks. Therefore the finding misreads the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to the datetime key, so value cursors break and navigation falls back to offset-only pagination, making deep pages O(offset) scans (the reverse of the promised optimization).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` which does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then applies `math.floor/ceil` and `int(...)` to that value. In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized paginator is used with `order_by="-datetime"`, implying the key will be a `datetime` field. Applying `math.floor/ceil` to a `datetime` is not valid and would raise a `TypeError` or otherwise produce incorrect cursor keys, breaking cursor-based navigation. The finding’s claim about “falling back to offset-only pagination” isn’t shown in the diff, but the core issue (incorrect key handling for datetime) is a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The negative-offset path does not make pagination more efficient: Django rejects negative slicing, so the "optimized" path gives no speedup and just adds a query that fails.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, and then slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (around line ~880). The earlier change to the existing paginator also allows `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev` (so it can also become negative). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices; attempting `queryset[-5:10]` will error rather than provide an optimization. So this diff introduces a real failure mode (a bad cursor with negative offset can break pagination) while claiming it's a performance optimization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — "Admin" gate uses member.has_global_access, which ordinary members of open-membership orgs have, and raises AttributeError (500) when member is None for non-member superuser/staff paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None-check. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` for some request paths (e.g., a user accessing via elevated privileges but not actually a member), then when `request.user.is_superuser` is false the RHS will be evaluated and can raise `AttributeError`, producing a 500. This risk is created by the new gating logic in `organization_auditlogs.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — User-controlled negative cursor offset is passed straight into queryset slicing, with a comment claiming it "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds"; Django rejects negative indexing so this is a client-triggerable 500/DoS and an unsafe bounds bypass.
matched_golden_ids: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: a negative cursor/offset ends up being used as a slice on a Django queryset. Django querysets don’t support negative slicing/indexing and will raise an AssertionError, producing a 500. The candidate points to the paginator implementation file rather than organization_auditlogs.py, but it’s the same root cause.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now passes unvalidated negative offsets for prev cursors into queryset slicing on every paginated endpoint, letting any caller trigger server errors via a crafted cursor.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the updated `get_result` now clamps `offset` to `>=0` only when `not cursor.is_prev`, but for `prev` cursors it uses `start_offset = offset` directly and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Since `Cursor.offset` is now explicitly described as allowing negative offsets (and is just `int(offset)` in `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py`), a crafted cursor with `is_prev=true` and a negative `offset` will flow into Django queryset slicing. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing/indexing and typically raise errors, so this can cause server errors on any endpoint using this paginator path. The newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator` also intentionally allows negative slicing when `enable_advanced_features` is set, reinforcing the same risky behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — Cursor parsing still accepts negative offsets from untrusted input with no bounds validation, which the new paginator code relies on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly enables/relies on negative cursor offsets: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`. Meanwhile `Cursor.__init__` still does `self.offset = int(offset)` with no bounds checks, so untrusted request cursors can supply negative offsets. This can produce invalid/unsupported queryset slicing and broken behavior (likely server errors) rather than being safely constrained.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator ships with no unit tests covering forward/prev paging, negative offsets, or enable_advanced_features toggle.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new pagination logic (new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class with `enable_advanced_features` behavior and negative-offset slicing paths in `get_result`) and changes audit log endpoint behavior to optionally use it, but the PR diff shows no accompanying test additions/updates covering forward/prev paging, negative offsets, or the feature toggle paths. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/coverage concern rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — No test exercises negative cursor offsets, which Django querysets reject (AssertionError "Negative indexing is not supported") so the advanced path would 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a code path that can slice a Django QuerySet with a negative start index. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and typically raises an AssertionError, so this path can 500 if a negative offset cursor is provided (the Cursor class now also documents allowing negative offsets).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator slicing behavior changed for all paginators (negative offset allowed when is_prev) without any regression test for prev cursors with negative offset.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` logic was changed from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which means for `cursor.is_prev` the paginator will now pass through a potentially negative `offset` directly into queryset slicing. This is a cross-cutting behavioral change affecting all paginators using `BasePaginator.get_result`, and the diff does not include any corresponding regression/behavioral tests covering `is_prev` cursors with negative offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removal of start/end/statsPeriod date filtering is a behavioral regression with no test update; existing date-range audit log tests would break or silently lose coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `organization_auditlogs.py` only changes pagination behavior (adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator` behind a query param/permission gate) and does not remove or modify any start/end/statsPeriod date filtering logic. There is no shown deletion of date-range filters or related tests in the provided diff, so the finding misreads the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Admin gate (is_superuser or member.has_global_access) is untested, including a non-superuser with no member record (member None -> AttributeError).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. This directly dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None-check; if `member` can ever be `None` for an authenticated non-superuser request, it would raise `AttributeError`. The diff alone doesn’t show whether the endpoint’s permission layer guarantees `organization_context.member` is always present, so the crash scenario isn’t fully verifiable, but the new logic does create a concrete potential edge-case that should be guarded and/or covered by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — No endpoint test verifies optimized_pagination=true is ignored for non-admin members and returns the same rows/ordering as DateTimePaginator.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial branching behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` based on the `optimized_pagination=true` query param and an admin-only gate (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`). For non-admin members, the code is intended to fall back to `DateTimePaginator` in the `else` branch. No corresponding test changes are shown in the diff to verify this gate (i.e., that non-admins cannot trigger `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and that results/ordering match the legacy `DateTimePaginator` path), making the review comment a specific, diff-grounded missing-coverage concern rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 — Prev-page trimming compares len(results) to offset+limit+extra, which is wrong for negative offsets, and no test covers result-count/has_results correctness on prev pages.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the prev-page trimming logic uses `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` where `offset` is `cursor.offset`. When advanced features allow negative offsets (`start_offset = cursor.offset`), `offset + limit + extra` no longer reflects the slice length (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), so the `results = results[:-1]` trimming branch can behave incorrectly (or fail to trigger) on prev pages. This defect is directly introduced by the diff’s negative-offset support and is not reconciled with the existing trimming condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses int(floor(value)) on a datetime key ("-datetime") which would TypeError; no test paginates audit logs through this class to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In the endpoint, the optimized path paginates audit logs with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)` before casting to `int`, which will raise `TypeError` if `value` is a `datetime` (as it would be when the key corresponds to `datetime`). This broken behavior is directly enabled by the diff via the new `optimized_pagination=true` flag path.
